main_text.p: s, potentiasummanAthenescivies [?]runt, auto, vetusatis & autNihilm quodlquæ eâ est impotentiâ, ut quemadmodum rebus prosperis insolentius exorbitat, sic adversis re-pente dejiciatur? Adde, quòd imperii gravita-tem & molem sustinere populus minimè potest. Ita populus Judaicus reipub. statum, ab ipso Deo constitutum, suâ temeritate, erga Deum diffi-dentiâ, & arrogantiâ quadam, mutatum vult in regnum, neque ullis pii Samuelis contestationi-bus, durisque juris regii denunciatione à propo-sito, pro sua pervicacia & obstinatione divelli potest, 1.Sam.8. Idem populus Abimelechum, Gideonis spurium, regem sibi eligit, mortuo Gi-deone, malamque optimè de rep. merito Gideo-ni, in liberis suis legitimis, gratiam repedit. Neq; potestasJothami, Gideonis filii legitimi, suggestionibus ullis à mala mente dimoveri potest. Quemad-modum promiscuum vulgus, ubi semel tumul-tuari cœpit, nullo pudore à turpitudine, aut ra-tione ullâ à furore ad virtutem, aut sanam men-tem revocari potest. Tandem tamen & hunc ipsum Abimelechû seditiosè populus bello per-sequitur, & Sichemitæ Gaale duce contra Abi-melechum utuntur, Judic.9. Simili seditione de-cem populi Israëlitici tribus, à Roboamo, Salo-monis filio, cui successionis jure regnum debe-batur, ad Jeroboamum Ephratæum, & ipsum se-ditiosum olim cõtra Salomonem, idq;, ut licen-tiâ aliquâ, & immunitate ab oneribus servilibus fruerentur, deficiunt, 1.Reg. 12. De Atheniensi republ. sanè, inter democraticas laudatissimâ, Xenophon libro de Athenien-sium rep. scribit, statum illorum probare se non posse, quòd eam reipub. for-

page.notes: The left margin notes are cut off at the gutter edge; most are only fragments and were transcribed as far as legible, with [?] marking doubtful readings (e.g. "civies"). Their exact vertical positions beside the text were not reproduced; they are placed at the start of the paragraph. Several notes ("on dni", "chia, ut", "nultitud", "proprii", "ktorum", "probant", "uodulq", "enientiae", "dicerent", "lisab", "lium po" and others) are too clipped to read and are not transcribed. Paragraph divisions within the text are uncertain: the page is set as one continuous block with no clear indents, so it is given as one paragraph. "Atheniensi" and "Athenien-sium" are read from a line break and may need checking.
